current_answer: As of 14 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven. The new independent evidence is mixed rather than exculpatory: Artificial Analysis reports Astra materially ahead of GPT-5.6 Sol on several intelligence and coding measures but about 45 Elo lower on GDPval-AA v2 and lower presentation-quality Elo; a same-model Astra-26 study shows tool stack and call budget can swing results. Current Codex reports add capacity errors despite displayed quota, session-persistent browser failures, and tool-output races; an independent one-account observatory estimates Astra consumes more quota per task despite fewer tokens. Specific capability slices, context/tool behavior, product, access, and economics can move separately. Audit context, served model, tool lifecycle, artifact, and allowance before switching.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: No broad decline is proven, but “not worse” is too simple: Astra leads several independent tests while trailing Sol on one work benchmark, and Codex users still report capacity, tool, and quota failures. Trace the surface before you switch.

summary: No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven, but the new evidence is mixed rather than cleanly reassuring.

Artificial Analysis reports Astra ahead of Sol on several intelligence and coding measures while about 45 Elo lower on GDPval-AA v2 and lower on presentation quality; this is cross-sectional, not a temporal decline test.
Astra-26 holds the model and broad task setup constant while search backends produce 42.3% to 23.1% reported accuracy, showing why tool stack and call budget belong in the comparison.

Fresh Codex reports describe capacity errors despite displayed allowance, session-persistent browser failure, and a tool-output race that can wedge a thread. These are product, access, and transport leads.
A one-account quota observatory estimates Astra uses more quota per task despite fewer tokens; it measures no answer quality and has no provider ledger.

OpenAI, Google Cloud, and Grok status records do not show a broad active incident in the checked snapshot; Claude Cowork remains degraded on Windows. Status is availability evidence, not quality evidence.
Reader move: audit context, record the served model and tool lifecycle, verify the artifact, and reconcile allowance before switching.
uncertainty: Artificial Analysis and Astra-26 are cross-sectional or harness-specific and do not establish a temporal weights decline.
Fresh Codex incidents are self-selected issue reports with no prevalence or independent reproduction.
The quota observatory covers one account and no task-quality outcome; provider allowance weighting is unknown.
Status pages are aggregate snapshots; no public matched longitudinal cross-provider capability series or first-party audience analytics is available.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source check completed 14 September 2026. Independent benchmark results now show a real mixed task-slice picture; current access, tool, and quota reports show why capability, availability, affordability, and verifiability must remain separate.
